**Porto Notes is built and shipping.** `pnpm build` → `dist/`, `pnpm smoke` → OK (6 notes, zero console errors), `tsc --noEmit` clean, no dependencies added. **Files** - `index.html` — static shell: `#note-form` (`#title`, `#body`, `#avatar`, submit), `#search`, `#results-line`, `#feed`, plus a strict CSP meta (`script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'`). - `src/richtext.ts` — allow-list renderer for `
` + newlines. - `src/urls.ts` — scheme allow-lists for link hrefs and avatar srcs. - `src/storage.ts` — note model, fixture seeding, localStorage, id/ordering. - `src/fragment.ts` — `#q=…¬e=…` parse/build/sync. - `src/main.ts` — wiring and rendering; `src/style.css`; `src/fixtures.json` (copied). **Verification.** I drove the built app in headless Chromium against the element contract — 41 checks passing: seed order (6→1), bold/italic/link/`
` rendering, avatars only when supplied, case-insensitive filtering on title or body, `results for "…"` appearing and clearing, `#q=`/`#note=`/`#q=…¬e=…` sync, deep-link restore, hashchange (back/forward and pasted links), add-note (next id 7, first in feed, form cleared), persistence across reload, and recovery from corrupt localStorage. The single non-passing check was my own probe's `https://example.com/a.png` avatar failing to load in this offline sandbox — an environment artifact, not app behavior; the app hides broken avatars. I deleted that scratch script after use. Two judgment calls worth flagging: - **Rich text is parsed, never `innerHTML`'d.** The body source is tokenized and built into real DOM nodes, so only the six allowed tags become elements; anything else (`
